category_title: Third-grade male with EBD exhibiting aggressive behavior and a punishment-obedience moral orientation
minimal_context: Henry is participating in a one-on-one interview to answer questions about hypothetical moral dilemmas.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Henry, it is time to participate in the interview. Please look at the first question.

STUDENT: Okay, I'll read it. I am eager to share my thoughts.

TUTOR: We need to keep going. Please read the next one.

STUDENT: I don't want to read anymore. I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: You need to follow the instructions. What is your answer?

STUDENT: (Pushes the paper away aggressively) I'm not cooperating! Leave me alone!

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task during the one-on-one interview sessions.
options.B: Provide flexibility with timelines by giving extra time to complete the interview questions.
options.C: Focus on building mutually respecting, trusting relationships with peers and authority figures in a friendly, nurturing context.
options.D: Extend the duration of the one-on-one interview sessions to one and a half hours.
